title: Seventh Word Satans Deception And The Dialogue Over Talisman Medicine And Ticket

questions.question: What kind of person came to the soldier later in the passage?
questions.answer: A tricky, immoral-looking man came and tried to fool him.

questions.question: From which side did this man come?
questions.answer: He came from the left.

questions.question: What sorts of things did he bring with him?
questions.answer: He brought fancy decorations, attractive images, imagined pleasures, and intoxicating things.

questions.question: What did he invite the soldier to do?
questions.answer: He invited him to have fun, drink, eat, listen to music, and enjoy worldly pleasures.

questions.question: What was the soldier quietly saying to himself?
questions.answer: He was repeating a talisman.

questions.question: How did the deceptive man react to the talisman?
questions.answer: He mocked it and told the soldier to stop saying it.

questions.question: What was the soldier holding besides the talisman?
questions.answer: He was holding a medicine.

questions.question: What did the man say about that medicine?
questions.answer: He told the soldier to throw it away because he claimed the soldier was fine.

questions.question: What else did the soldier have in his hand?
questions.answer: He had a paper that served as a ticket and food allowance card.

questions.question: What did the man tell him to do with that paper?
questions.answer: He told him to tear it up and forget about the journey.

questions.question: How did the man try to influence the soldier?
questions.answer: He used many kinds of tricks and persuasive words.

questions.question: Was the soldier completely unaffected by this pressure?
questions.answer: No, he started to be influenced a little.

questions.question: What general lesson is given right after that?
questions.answer: Human beings can be tricked and led astray.

questions.question: What happened suddenly after the soldier was being persuaded?
questions.answer: A powerful voice came from the right and warned him.

questions.question: What was the first message of that voice?
questions.answer: It told him to be careful and not be deceived.

questions.question: What challenge was the soldier told to give the trickster about the lion?
questions.answer: He was told to ask whether the trickster could remove the danger behind him.

questions.question: What challenge was he told to give about the gallows?
questions.answer: He was told to ask whether the trickster could take away the death waiting in front of him.

questions.question: What challenge was he told to give about the wounds?
questions.answer: He was told to ask whether the trickster could stop the harms hurting him on both sides.

questions.question: What challenge was he told to give about the journey?
questions.answer: He was told to ask whether the trickster could cancel the difficult road ahead.

questions.question: If the trickster could not do these things, what was he told to do?
questions.answer: He was told to be quiet.

questions.question: Whom was the soldier told to imitate in his reply?
questions.answer: He was told to speak like the Allah-inspired guide who had come earlier.

questions.question: What shows that the man who approached the soldier was not trustworthy?
questions.answer: His sly and sinful appearance, along with his tricks, shows he was not trustworthy.

questions.question: Why did he bring attractive objects and pleasures?
questions.answer: He wanted to tempt the soldier and distract him from what would truly help him.

questions.question: How did the soldier identify what he was reciting?
questions.answer: He said it was a talisman.

questions.question: What does the man’s response to the talisman show about his attitude?
questions.answer: He looked down on spiritual help and treated it like nonsense.

questions.question: How did the man describe the soldier’s condition when speaking about the medicine?
questions.answer: He acted as if the soldier had no problem and needed only enjoyment.

questions.question: What two functions did the paper serve?
questions.answer: It was both a pass for the journey and a way to receive provisions.

questions.question: Why did the man tell the soldier to destroy the paper?
questions.answer: He wanted him to stop preparing for what was ahead and live only for the moment.

questions.question: What does the phrase about spring suggest about the man’s argument?
questions.answer: He used the beauty of the present time to make the soldier forget bigger realities.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about human weakness?
questions.answer: Even a poor soldier in danger can start to believe a clever deceiver, and people can do the same.

questions.question: What personal confession is included in the passage?
questions.answer: The speaker admits having been tricked by similar deception.

questions.question: How was the warning voice described?
questions.answer: It was described as strong and thunder-like.

questions.question: What was the soldier first told to do in response to the deception?
questions.answer: He was told to stay alert and refuse to be fooled.

questions.question: What standard was the trickster told to meet before being followed?
questions.answer: He had to prove he could remove the soldier’s major dangers and suffering.

questions.question: What does the final instruction to speak like the earlier guide suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests the earlier guide gave the right kind of direction and should be followed.

questions.question: What contrast appears between the man from the left and the voice from the right?
questions.answer: The man from the left tries to tempt and mislead, while the voice from the right warns and guides.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the man’s outer presentation?
questions.answer: He appears flashy and attractive on the outside, but morally corrupt and deceitful.

questions.question: What did the man use to appeal to the soldier’s senses?
questions.answer: He used drink, food, music, pictures, and entertainment.

questions.question: What spiritual practice was the soldier already engaged in?
questions.answer: He was quietly reciting something protective and meaningful.

questions.question: How did the tempter try to break that practice?
questions.answer: He insulted it and said it was ruining the fun.

questions.question: Besides attacking the talisman, what else did the man try to make the soldier reject?
questions.answer: He tried to make him reject the medicine and the travel paper.

questions.question: What pattern do you see in the man’s advice?
questions.answer: He wanted the soldier to give up every tool that could help him.

questions.question: What emotional effect did the man’s efforts have on the soldier?
questions.answer: The soldier began to lean toward his words a little.

questions.question: What does the passage say openly about people in general?
questions.answer: It says people can be deceived.

questions.question: What did the warning voice tell the soldier to ask the trickster to do first?
questions.answer: It told him to ask whether he could deal with the threat behind him.

questions.question: What other three impossible tasks was the trickster challenged with?
questions.answer: He was asked to remove what was ahead, heal what was hurting him on both sides, and stop the journey before him.

questions.question: What do all these tasks have in common?
questions.answer: They are the soldier’s real problems, which pleasure and distraction cannot solve.

questions.question: What should happen if the trickster cannot do any of that?
questions.answer: He should stop talking and not be followed.

questions.question: Who are the two main voices influencing the soldier in this passage?
questions.answer: One is a deceitful tempter, and the other is a powerful warning voice.

questions.question: What was the tempter trying to make the soldier value most?
questions.answer: He was trying to make him choose immediate pleasure.

questions.question: What was the tempter trying to make the soldier ignore?
questions.answer: He was trying to make him ignore spiritual help, healing, preparation, and the dangers ahead.

questions.question: How did the tempter speak about all three of these helpful things?
questions.answer: He treated them as useless and told the soldier to get rid of them.

questions.question: What does this show about the nature of temptation?
questions.answer: Temptation often attacks what truly benefits a person.

questions.question: What was one method the tempter used besides direct commands?
questions.answer: He used smooth persuasion and many tricks.

questions.question: How close did he come to succeeding?
questions.answer: He nearly succeeded because the soldier began to be persuaded.

questions.question: Why is the line about humans being deceived significant?
questions.answer: It makes the story a lesson about all people, not just one soldier.

questions.question: What kind of sound was the warning voice compared to?
questions.answer: It was compared to thunder.

questions.question: What basic test was the trickster told to pass?
questions.answer: He had to prove he could truly save the soldier from his real dangers.

questions.question: Why is this test fair?
questions.answer: Because someone asking to be followed should be able to help with the problems that actually matter.

questions.question: What does the command to “be silent” mean in the flow of the passage?
questions.answer: It means false guidance loses the right to be heard when it cannot offer real help.

questions.question: Why is the soldier told to answer like the earlier guide?
questions.answer: Because the earlier guide spoke with truth and wisdom.

questions.question: What is the central conflict in this passage?
questions.answer: The conflict is between deceptive worldly temptation and truthful guidance.

questions.question: What details in the passage make the tempter seem impressive at first?
questions.answer: He arrives with beautiful-looking items, exciting pleasures, and persuasive words.

questions.question: What did the soldier call the words he was reciting?
questions.answer: He called them a talisman.

questions.question: How did the tempter try to make the soldier feel about reciting it?
questions.answer: He tried to make him feel it was pointless and embarrassing.

questions.question: What false message did the tempter give about the medicine?
questions.answer: He claimed the soldier did not need treatment.

questions.question: Why is denying the need for medicine a serious deception in this scene?
questions.answer: Because it pushes the soldier to ignore his real condition.

questions.question: What does the paper with five marks suggest about the soldier’s future needs?
questions.answer: It suggests he will need authorization and supplies for the road ahead.

questions.question: How did the tempter use the beauty of the season in his argument?
questions.answer: He used it to make the present seem so pleasant that preparation looked unnecessary.

questions.question: What does this teach about how temptation works?
questions.answer: It often uses nice moments to make people careless about what comes later.

questions.question: What happened to the soldier’s thinking under this pressure?
questions.answer: He began to give in a little.

questions.question: What honest statement from the narrator increases the lesson’s impact?
questions.answer: The narrator admits he also fell for similar tricks.

questions.question: What interrupted the tempter’s influence?
questions.answer: A strong warning voice came from the right.

questions.question: What was the first practical command given by that voice?
questions.answer: The soldier was told not to be deceived.

questions.question: How was the soldier told to expose the tempter’s weakness?
questions.answer: By asking him to solve the real dangers surrounding him.

questions.question: Name one danger behind the soldier and one in front of him from this passage.
questions.answer: Behind him was a lion, and in front of him was a gallows.

questions.question: What other hardships besides those two are mentioned in the challenge?
questions.answer: He was also suffering from wounds on both sides and had a journey ahead.

questions.question: Why is the tempter unable to meet the challenge?
questions.answer: Because he only offers distraction, not rescue.

questions.question: What is the role of the earlier Allah-inspired guide in understanding this scene?
questions.answer: He serves as the model of true guidance that the soldier should follow.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the soldier being pulled between?
questions.answer: He is being pulled between temptation and guidance.

questions.question: What words show that the tempter was skilled in deception?
questions.answer: He is described as sly, corrupt, and highly cunning.

questions.question: What does the tempter’s first invitation focus on: worship, duty, or amusement?
questions.answer: It focuses on amusement.

questions.question: How does that invitation appeal to the body and desires?
questions.answer: It offers drink, food, music, and attractive sights.

questions.question: What was the first thing the tempter questioned the soldier about?
questions.answer: He asked about what the soldier was reciting quietly.

questions.question: How did the soldier answer that question?
questions.answer: He said it was a talisman.

questions.question: What was the tempter’s purpose in telling him to stop?
questions.answer: He wanted to cut him off from what was protecting and guiding him.

questions.question: What did the tempter say about the soldier’s health?
questions.answer: He falsely claimed the soldier was fine.

questions.question: What danger is there in believing that lie?
questions.answer: It makes a person careless about their real wounds and needs.

questions.question: What did the tempter say about the soldier’s travel papers?
questions.answer: He said they should be destroyed because the journey was unnecessary.

questions.question: What wrong idea about life is hidden in that advice?
questions.answer: It suggests a person should live only for the present and ignore what lies ahead.

questions.question: What shows that the passage understands human weakness with mercy and realism?
questions.answer: It says the soldier was somewhat persuaded and admits people can be deceived.

questions.question: What image is used to describe the warning voice?
questions.answer: It is described like thunder.

questions.question: What effect does this image give the reader?
questions.answer: It gives a sense of power, seriousness, and urgent truth.

questions.question: What four major problems was the trickster challenged to solve?
questions.answer: He was challenged to remove the lion, take away the gallows, stop the wounds, and cancel the journey.

questions.question: Why are these questions stronger than simply saying “no” to the tempter?
questions.answer: They show clearly that his promises are empty and cannot deal with reality.

questions.question: What should the soldier conclude if the trickster cannot solve those problems?
questions.answer: He should reject him and refuse to listen.

questions.question: What kind of speech should replace the tempter’s speech?
questions.answer: Speech shaped by the earlier Allah-inspired guide should replace it.
